text: Which of the following is the final product of $\text{Anaerobic}$ $\text{Respiration}$ in $\text{Yeast}$?
image: [Diagram of alcoholic fermentation process]
explanation: In $\text{Yeast}$ (a fungus), $\text{Anaerobic}$ $\text{Respiration}$ is known as $\text{Alcoholic}$ $\text{Fermentation}$, producing $\text{Ethanol}$, $\text{Carbon}$ $\text{Dioxide}$ ($\text{CO}_2$), and a small amount of $\text{Energy}$ ($\text{ATP}$). $\text{Lactic}$ $\text{Acid}$ is the product in animal muscles.

text: The structure in the $\text{Cell}$ that controls the passage of substances into and out of the cell is the:
image: [Diagram of the Fluid Mosaic Model of the Cell Membrane]
explanation: The $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Membrane}$ ($	ext{Plasma}$ $\text{Membrane}$) is $\text{Selectively}$ $\text{Permeable}$ and controls what enters and leaves the cell, ensuring $\text{Homeostasis}$.

text: The $\text{Organ}$ in the human body that produces $\text{Bile}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of the Human Liver and Gall Bladder]
explanation: The $\text{Liver}$ produces $\text{Bile}$, which is then stored and concentrated in the $\text{Gall}$ $\text{Bladder}$ before being released into the $\text{Small}$ $\text{Intestine}$.

text: The part of the plant embryo that develops into the $\text{Shoot}$ $\text{System}$ (stem and leaves) is the:
image: [Diagram of seed germination showing Plumule and Radicle]
explanation: The $\text{Plumule}$ is the embryonic $\text{Shoot}$ that develops into the aerial $\text{Parts}$ (stem and leaves). The $\text{Radicle}$ develops into the $\text{Root}$.

text: Which of the following is $\text{NOT}$ a primary function of the $\text{Skeleton}$ in mammals?
image: [Diagram of the human skeletal system]
explanation: The $\text{Skeleton}$ (bone tissue) provides $\text{Support}$, $\text{Protection}$, $\text{Leverage}$ for movement (locomotion), and produces $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Cells}$ in the $\text{Bone}$ $\text{Marrow}$. Hormone production is primarily the role of $\text{Endocrine}$ $\text{Glands}$.

text: The process by which organisms maintain a constant internal environment despite changes in the external environment is known as:
image: [Simple feedback loop diagram for Homeostasis (e.g., temperature regulation)]
explanation: $\text{Homeostasis}$ is the maintenance of a relatively stable internal condition (e.g., $\text{Temperature}$, $\text{Glucose}$ $\text{Level}$, $\text{pH}$) in the body.

text: The instrument used to measure the $\text{Relative}$ $\text{Humidity}$ of the atmosphere is the:
explanation: A $\text{Hygrometer}$ (or $\text{Psychrometer}$) is a meteorological instrument used to measure the amount of $\text{Water}$ $\text{Vapour}$ in the air ($	ext{Humidity}$). An $\text{Anemometer}$ measures $\text{Wind}$ $\text{Speed}$.

text: The main substance that constitutes the $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Wall}$ of plant cells is:
image: [Microscopic view of plant cell walls]
explanation: Plant $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Walls}$ are primarily composed of $\text{Cellulose}$, a complex carbohydrate. $\text{Chitin}$ forms the cell walls of $\text{Fungi}$.

text: A population is defined as a group of organisms of:
image: [Diagram illustrating a population of a single species in a defined area]
explanation: In $\text{Ecology}$, a $\text{Population}$ is defined as all the members of $\text{One}$ $\text{Specific}$ $\text{Species}$ living in a $\text{Particular}$ $\text{Geographical}$ $\text{Area}$ at a given time.

text: Which of the following blood components is responsible for $\text{Clotting}$?
image: [Microscopic image of Platelets]
explanation: $\text{Platelets}$ are small, irregular cell fragments that initiate the $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Clotting}$ cascade by releasing $\text{Thromboplastin}$ when a blood vessel is damaged.

text: The type of $\text{Circulatory}$ $\text{System}$ found in $\text{Insects}$ (e.g., grasshopper) is:
image: [Diagram comparing open and closed circulatory systems]
explanation: $\text{Insects}$ and most other $\text{Arthropods}$ have an $\text{Open}$ $\text{Circulatory}$ $\text{System}$, where $\text{Blood}$ ($	ext{Haemolymph}$) is pumped into a cavity ($	ext{Haemocoel}$) and bathes the organs directly, rather than being confined solely to vessels.

text: The part of the $\text{Flower}$ that attracts $\text{Insects}$ for $\text{Pollination}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of a flower showing petals]
explanation: The $\text{Petals}$ are typically large, brightly $\text{Coloured}$, and often scented, making them the main attractive structure for $\text{Insect}$ $\text{Pollinators}$.

text: Which hormone is associated with the conversion of excess $\text{Glucose}$ into $\text{Glycogen}$ in the $\text{Liver}$?
image: [Diagram showing Insulin's role in glucose uptake and storage]
explanation: $\text{Insulin}$, secreted by the $\text{Pancreas}$, $\text{Lowers}$ $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Glucose}$ $\text{Level}$ by promoting the uptake of glucose by body cells and the conversion of glucose into $\text{Glycogen}$ ($	ext{Glycogenesis}$) for storage in the $\text{Liver}$ and $\text{Muscles}$.

text: The phenomenon where an organism is better suited to survive and reproduce in its environment is called:
image: [Image illustrating Natural Selection in peppered moths]
explanation: An $\text{Adaptation}$ is any $\text{Heritable}$ $\text{Trait}$ (structural, physiological, or behavioral) that increases an organism's $\text{Fitness}$ (survival and reproductive success) in its specific environment.

text: The organ of $\text{Sight}$ in humans contains $\text{Receptors}$ known as:
image: [Diagram of the Human Eye showing Rods and Cones]
explanation: $\text{Rods}$ and $\text{Cones}$ are the two types of $\text{Photoreceptors}$ located in the $\text{Retina}$ of the eye. $\text{Rods}$ are for $\text{Dim}$ $\text{Light}$ (black/white), and $\text{Cones}$ are for $\text{Bright}$ $\text{Light}$ and $\text{Colour}$ $\text{Vision}$.

text: The part of the $\text{Skin}$ responsible for cooling the body through the evaporation of sweat is the:
image: [Cross-section diagram of the Human Skin showing a Sweat Gland]
explanation: The $\text{Sweat}$ $\text{Glands}$ secrete sweat, which evaporates from the skin surface, drawing $\text{Heat}$ $\text{Energy}$ from the body and thus cooling it (a process of $\text{Thermoregulation}$).

text: In $\text{Genetics}$, $\text{Homologous}$ $\text{Chromosomes}$ are best described as a pair of chromosomes that:
image: [Diagram of homologous chromosomes]
options: Are $\text{Similar}$ in $\text{Size}$ and carry $\text{Genes}$ for the $\text{Same}$ $\text{Traits}$
answer: Are $\text{Similar}$ in $\text{Size}$ and carry $\text{Genes}$ for the $\text{Same}$ $\text{Traits}$
explanation: $\text{Homologous}$ $\text{Chromosomes}$ are one from each parent that are $\text{Similar}$ in $\text{Length}$ and $\text{Gene}$ $\text{Position}$ (loci), but may carry $\text{Different}$ $\text{Alleles}$ for those genes.

text: The $\text{Movement}$ of water molecules across a $\text{Selectively}$ $\text{Permeable}$ $\text{Membrane}$ from a region of $\text{Higher}$ $\text{Water}$ $\text{Potential}$ to a region of $\text{Lower}$ $\text{Water}$ $\text{Potential}$ is called:
image: [Diagram illustrating Osmosis in different concentration solutions]
explanation: $\text{Osmosis}$ is the specific type of $\text{Diffusion}$ that involves only the $\text{Movement}$ of $\text{Water}$ $\text{Molecules}$ across a $\text{Semipermeable}$ $\text{Membrane}$.

text: The essential gaseous reactant for $\text{Photosynthesis}$ in plants is:
image: [Equation for Photosynthesis]
explanation: $\text{Carbon}$ $\text{Dioxide}$ ($	ext{CO}_2$) is fixed and used, along with $\text{Water}$ and $\text{Light}$ $\text{Energy}$, to produce $\text{Glucose}$ and $\text{Oxygen}$ during $\text{Photosynthesis}$.

text: Which of the following classes of $\text{Vertebrates}$ are generally characterized by having $\text{Scales}$, laying $\text{Shelled}$ $\text{Eggs}$ on land, and being $\text{Ectothermic}$?
image: [Image showing examples of Reptiles]
explanation: $\text{Reptiles}$ (snakes, lizards, crocodiles, tortoises) are typically $\text{Ectothermic}$ (cold-blooded), have dry, $\text{Scaled}$ $\text{Skin}$ to prevent water loss, and reproduce by laying $\text{Amniotic}$ (shelled) $\text{Eggs}$ on $\text{Land}$.

text: In the $\text{Food}$ $\text{Chain}$: Grass $\rightarrow$ Grasshopper $\rightarrow$ Lizard $\rightarrow$ Hawk, the Lizard is the:
image: [Diagram of the Food Chain and Trophic Levels]
explanation: Grass ($\text{Producer}$) $\rightarrow$ Grasshopper ($\text{Primary}$ $\text{Consumer}$) $\rightarrow$ Lizard ($\text{Secondary}$ $\text{Consumer}$ - eats primary) $\rightarrow$ Hawk ($\text{Tertiary}$ $\text{Consumer}$ - eats secondary). The lizard eats the grasshopper.

text: A viral disease that is typically transmitted through $\text{Sexual}$ $\text{Contact}$ is:
image: [Symbolic representation of HIV virus]
explanation: $\text{AIDS}$ is caused by the $\text{Human}$ $\text{Immunodeficiency}$ $\text{Virus}$ ($\text{HIV}$), which is transmitted primarily through $\text{Unprotected}$ $\text{Sexual}$ $\text{Intercourse}$, blood transfusions, and from mother to child.

text: The $\text{Enzyme}$ that breaks down $\text{Protein}$ into $\text{Polypeptides}$ in the $\text{Stomach}$ is:
image: [Diagram illustrating the action of Pepsin]
explanation: $\text{Pepsin}$ is a $\text{Protease}$ enzyme secreted in the $\text{Stomach}$ (as $\text{Pepsinogen}$) and activated by $\text{Hydrochloric}$ $\text{Acid}$. It begins the digestion of $\text{Proteins}$ into smaller $\text{Polypeptide}$ chains.

text: The relationship between a $\text{Tick}$ and a $\text{Cow}$, where the tick benefits by feeding on the cow's blood and the cow is harmed, is an example of:
image: [Image illustrating Parasitism (Tick on a host)]
explanation: $\text{Parasitism}$ is a symbiotic relationship where one organism (the $\text{Parasite}$ - the $\text{Tick}$) $\text{Benefits}$ at the expense of the other (the $\text{Host}$ - the $\text{Cow}$). $\text{Ticks}$ are $\text{Ectoparasites}$.

text: Which structure in the $\text{Ear}$ converts $\text{Sound}$ $\text{Vibrations}$ into $\text{Nerve}$ $\text{Impulses}$?
image: [Cross-section of the Inner Ear highlighting the Cochlea]
explanation: The $\text{Cochlea}$ in the $\text{Inner}$ $\text{Ear}$ contains $\text{Sensory}$ $\text{Hair}$ $\text{Cells}$ that convert the fluid waves generated by sound vibrations into $\text{Electrical}$ $\text{Nerve}$ $\text{Signals}$ sent to the brain.

text: A plant is considered a $\text{Xerophyte}$ if it is adapted to survive in an environment with:
explanation: $\text{Xerophytes}$ are plants that have specialized morphological and physiological adaptations (like $\text{Thick}$ $\text{Cuticles}$, $\text{Sunken}$ $\text{Stomata}$, or $\text{Fleshy}$ $\text{Stems}$) to survive in $\text{Arid}$ or $\text{Dry}$ habitats with $\text{Limited}$ $\text{Water}$ $\text{Availability}$.

text: In the process of $\text{Meiosis}$, $\text{Crossing}$ $\text{Over}$ occurs during:
image: [Diagram illustrating Crossing Over in Prophase I of Meiosis]
explanation: $\text{Crossing}$ $\text{Over}$ is the exchange of $\text{Genetic}$ $\text{Material}$ between $\text{Non}$-$\text{Sister}$ $\text{Chromatids}$ of $\text{Homologous}$ $\text{Chromosomes}$, which happens during $\text{Prophase}$ $\text{I}$ and contributes to $\text{Genetic}$ $\text{Variation}$.

text: The $\text{Small}$ $\text{Intestine}$ is highly adapted for $\text{Absorption}$ of digested food due to the presence of:
image: [Microscopic image of Villi in the small intestine]
explanation: The $\text{Villi}$ and $\text{Microvilli}$ are finger-like projections that greatly $\text{Increase}$ the $\text{Surface}$ $\text{Area}$ of the $\text{Small}$ $\text{Intestine}$, maximizing the efficiency of $\text{Nutrient}$ $\text{Absorption}$ into the bloodstream and lymph.

text: The main excretory product of $\text{Fish}$ and other aquatic organisms is:
image: [Diagram illustrating excretion of Ammonia]
explanation: $\text{Ammonia}$ is highly $\text{Toxic}$ but highly $\text{Soluble}$ in water, requiring large amounts of water for excretion. $\text{Aquatic}$ $\text{Animals}$ (e.g., $\text{Fish}$) can excrete it directly into the water, while $\text{Mammals}$ convert it to less toxic $\text{Urea}$.

text: Which of the following describes the $\text{Mouth}$ $\text{Parts}$ of a $\text{Mosquito}$?
image: [Diagram of Mosquito mouthparts (Piercing and Sucking)]
explanation: The $\text{Mosquito}$ (female) has specialized, needle-like $\text{Mouthparts}$ that are adapted for $\text{Piercing}$ the skin of a host and $\text{Sucking}$ $\text{Blood}$ (or plant sap).

text: The $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Organelle}$ primarily responsible for $\text{Aerobic}$ $\text{Respiration}$ and $\text{ATP}$ $\text{Production}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of a Mitochondrion (the powerhouse of the cell)]
explanation: The $\text{Mitochondrion}$ is often called the '$\text{Powerhouse}$' of the cell because the later stages of $\text{Aerobic}$ $\text{Respiration}$ ($	ext{Krebs}$ $\text{Cycle}$ and $\text{Oxidative}$ $\text{Phosphorylation}$) occur here, generating most of the cell's $\text{ATP}$.

text: The presence of $\text{Sexual}$ $\text{Dimorphism}$ in animals primarily indicates that:
image: [Image showing a Peacock and Peahen (Sexual Dimorphism)]
options: The male and female individuals of the species are $\text{Visually}$ $\text{Different}$
answer: The male and female individuals of the species are $\text{Visually}$ $\text{Different}$
explanation: $\text{Sexual}$ $\text{Dimorphism}$ refers to the systematic $\text{Difference}$ in form between $\text{Individuals}$ of $\text{Different}$ $\text{Sex}$ in the same species (e.g., size, colour, presence of horns/antlers, etc.).

text: In $\text{Plant}$ $\text{Hormones}$, $\text{Gibberellins}$ are primarily known for causing:
image: [Image illustrating Gibberellin application on a dwarf plant resulting in stem elongation]
explanation: $\text{Gibberellins}$ are plant hormones that play a major role in $\text{Stem}$ $\text{Elongation}$ (especially in dwarf plants) and stimulating $\text{Seed}$ $\text{Germination}$ and $\text{Flowering}$.

text: Which of these $\text{Vitamins}$ is essential for $\text{Normal}$ $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Clotting}$?
explanation: $\text{Vitamin}$ $\text{K}$ is crucial because it is required by the $\text{Liver}$ for the synthesis of several $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Clotting}$ $\text{Factors}$, most notably $\text{Prothrombin}$.

text: The accumulation of $\text{Non}$-$\text{Biodegradable}$ $\text{Substances}$ (like $\text{Pesticides}$) in the $\text{Food}$ $\text{Chain}$ is known as:
image: [Diagram illustrating Biomagnification in a food web]
explanation: $\text{Biomagnification}$ ($	ext{Bioaccumulation}$) is the $\text{Increase}$ in $\text{Concentration}$ of a $\text{Substance}$ (e.g., $\text{Heavy}$ $\text{Metals}$, $\text{DDT}$) in $\text{Organisms}$ at $\text{Higher}$ $\text{Trophic}$ $\text{Levels}$ in a food chain.

text: Which part of the $\text{Nephron}$ is primarily responsible for $\text{Ultrafiltration}$?
image: [Diagram of the Glomerulus and Bowman's Capsule]
explanation: The high $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Pressure}$ in the $\text{Glomerulus}$ forces water and small solutes out of the blood into the $\text{Bowman's}$ $\text{Capsule}$, a process known as $\text{Ultrafiltration}$.

text: A character that can be inherited and varies continuously among individuals (e.g., $\text{Height}$, $\text{Skin}$ $\text{Colour}$) is controlled by:
image: [Graph illustrating continuous variation (normal distribution curve)]
explanation: $\text{Continuous}$ $\text{Variation}$ is typically controlled by $\text{Polygenic}$ $\text{Inheritance}$, where $\text{Multiple}$ $\text{Genes}$ at different loci collectively influence a single $\text{Phenotypic}$ $\text{Trait}$.

text: Which of the following is an example of an $\text{Innate}$ (unlearned) $\text{Behaviour}$ in animals?
options: A $\text{Bird}$ building a $\text{Nest}$ for the first time
answer: A $\text{Bird}$ building a $\text{Nest}$ for the first time
explanation: Innate behaviors are $\text{Genetically}$ $\text{Programmed}$ and performed correctly the first time they are attempted, often referred to as $\text{Instincts}$ or $\text{Fixed}$ $\text{Action}$ $\text{Patterns}$ (like nest building).

text: The $\text{Epidermis}$ of a plant leaf is covered by a $\text{Waxy}$ $\text{Layer}$ called the:
image: [Cross-section of a leaf showing the waxy Cuticle]
explanation: The $\text{Cuticle}$ is a $\text{Waxy}$ $\text{Layer}$ that covers the outer $\text{Epidermal}$ $\text{Cells}$ of leaves and stems. Its primary function is to $\text{Reduce}$ $\text{Water}$ $\text{Loss}$ through $\text{Evaporation}$.

text: The $\text{Main}$ $\text{Function}$ of $\text{Red}$ $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Cells}$ (Erythrocytes) is the:
explanation: $\text{Red}$ $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Cells}$ contain $\text{Haemoglobin}$, which binds to $\text{Oxygen}$ in the $\text{Lungs}$ and releases it to the $\text{Tissues}$ of the body.
